# `misplaced-try`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: semantic · Profile: none · Default: error · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports `try` outside any function body, and `try` on a provably fallible call
in a function whose declared return type is not an error union; the compiler
rejects both.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`try` returns the error from the enclosing function, so it needs a function
that can return one. At container level, in a declaration's initializer or a
`comptime` block, there is no function and AstGen rejects it as "'try' outside
function scope". In a function whose return type is not an error union, the
compiler rejects any `try` whose operand can fail ("function cannot return an
error"). Both usually mean a forgotten `!` in the signature or an error that
should be handled in place.

## When it fires

It reports `try` outside every function and test body, and `try` in a
function whose declared return type is visibly not an error union (a
primitive such as `void` or `usize`, an optional, pointer or array type, or a
`struct`, `enum`, `union` or `opaque` declared in the file) when its operand
provably can fail: an allocator call (`alloc`, `create`, `dupe`, `realloc`,
...) or a call to a function of this file whose error set is a non-empty
`error{...}`, `anyerror`, or an inferred set fed by `return error.Name`. A
`try` with an empty or unknown error set compiles and is not reported, nor is
one inside `defer`, which the compiler reports separately.

For a container-level `const value = try load();` the quick fix writes
`load() catch unreachable`, which turns a comptime failure into a compile
error. In a function, it makes the return type an error union (`!usize`),
except for `export`, `extern` and `callconv` functions, which cannot return
one.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn duplicate(gpa: std.mem.Allocator, name: []const u8) []u8 {
    return try gpa.dupe(u8, name);
}
```
